item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL) in collaboration with Videotage, Hong Kong

Location: Residency takes place at Videotage in Hong Kong. Applicants must be established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands) and registered in a business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: EUR 5,000 for a two-month residency or EUR 6,500 for a three-month residency, paid by the Creative Industries Fund NL to cover travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Accommodation, use of the studio space and facilitation by Videotage are covered directly by the Fund on top of this. No application fee.

Duration: Two or three months in 2027 (spring 2027); state your preferred period in the application.

Deadline: 21 Oct 2026

The Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) runs this residency with Videotage, a Hong Kong-based non-profit media arts institution specialising in the promotion, presentation, creation and preservation of moving image and media art in all forms and languages. The Fund is recruiting one Netherlands-based designer, maker or observer working in digital culture to spend two or three months at Videotage's studio space in Hong Kong in 2027, conducting research, broadening their network, developing new work inspired by Hong Kong, and presenting their findings or completed works. The residency encourages crossovers and experimentation, giving the participant space to explore new methodologies, widen their creative practice and produce work that pushes the boundaries of digital culture, with a focus on social and urban dynamics. The 2027 edition takes the technological 'black box' phenomenon as its starting point and invites the resident to respond to that theme within the context of Videotage. ELIGIBILITY: you are an individual designer, maker or observer within the field of digital culture; you are established in the Netherlands, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao, Saba, Sint Eustatius or Sint Maarten (Kingdom of the Netherlands); you are registered in the business register of the Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) or another business register within the Kingdom of the Netherlands; and you have had a professional practice in the creative industry for at least four years. NOT open to duos, collectives or cooperative ventures, nor to designers and makers who receive a grant during the work period under the Talent Development Grant Scheme, the Open Call Self-taught Designer or the Open Call Emerging Design Practices ABCSSS. Note that accepting this open call means you cannot apply to those schemes and open calls in 2027. FUNDING: EUR 5,000 for two months or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested and material and transport costs; accommodation, studio use and Videotage's facilitation are covered separately by the Fund. Submit your proposal to the Creative Industries Fund NL by 21 October 2026, 16:00 CEST.

item.title: University of Twente: Postdoc, Ethics and Epistemology of LLMs4EU (17 months)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Twente, Philosophy section / 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology

Location: Enschede, Netherlands

Award: EUR 4,241 to 5,538 gross per month (scale 10, steps 4 to 12) at 1.0 FTE, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and an 8.3 percent year-end bonus.

Duration: 17 months, full-time (38 to 40 hours per week), with possible extension

Deadline: 25 Aug 2026

A postdoctoral position in the Philosophy section at the University of Twente, part of the 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology, working on the ethics and epistemology strand (Work Package 6) of LLMs4EU. LLMs4EU is a European Commission funded initiative led by the Alliance for Language Technologies, spanning more than 20 countries, to build large language models across all EU languages and preserve European linguistic and cultural diversity in the digital age while keeping the resulting tools compliant with European values and legislation including the AI Act and the GDPR. TASKS: establish benchmarking frameworks that address legal and ethical concerns; develop guidelines for fine-tuning processes with an emphasis on preserving cultural heritage; oversee ethics compliance and advise the project ethics board; and build frameworks that integrate ethical considerations into LLM design. This is the tech-communication and language-politics end of AI research rather than a modelling job: the questions are whose language, whose culture and whose norms get encoded when a continent builds its own models. REQUIREMENTS: a doctorate in ethics, philosophy, science and technology studies, AI ethics, computer science with an ethics focus, or a related field; demonstrated expertise in AI ethics and ethics compliance; understanding of AI tool design and LLM development; appreciation for cultural diversity; strong communication and organisational skills; and professional English. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting. Closes 25 August 2026.

Open call details

item.title: JUGAAD: Absolute Improvisation, open call for printed matter and small-format works (Amsterdam)
item.description:
Organisation: SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet

Location: Fair takes place 9-10 October 2026 in Amsterdam. Open internationally, but selected work must be shipped to the Netherlands by the end of September 2026 at the artist's expense.

Award: No application fee. Selected work is sold at the printed matter fair on mutually agreeable terms regarding commission, duration and number of editions; artists are remunerated within 30 days of each sale. Unsold works are returned at the end of the agreed consignment period.

Duration: Rolling selection 5 August to 5 September 2026; fair 9-10 October 2026

Deadline: 05 Sep 2026

Open call from SAC Art Amsterdam and Mama Magnet for a printed matter fair themed around jugaad: improvised, resourceful solutions built from what is on hand (from the Sanskrit yuj, 'to join', via Hindi jugar, famously embodied by post-independence Punjabi vehicles pieced together from scrap metal and pump engines). The curators want work that engages the spirit of jugaad either as subject (everyday intelligences of getting by, lateral logics of adaptation, unlikely workarounds, reinvention born of necessity) or in how it was made (found or repurposed materials, adapted processes, structures built to solve a specific constraint). Work that came from adjustment rather than access, problem-solving rather than budget. WHAT: zines, artist books, comics, risograph or photocopied prints, posters, foldables, instruction manuals, packaging and other small-format works; if it can travel in a suitcase it is probably in scope. No framed work or anything needing gallery-standard installation. Gen-AI images and text are not accepted. WHO: artists, designers, writers and collectives whose practice genuinely engages with the theme; if unsure, reach out and explain in a line or two. Selected work must reach the Netherlands by end of September 2026. TERMS: selections made on a rolling basis 5 August to 5 September; selected work is sold at the fair (9-10 October, Amsterdam) on mutually agreeable commission terms, with payment within 30 days of each sale and unsold work returned after the consignment period. HOW TO APPLY: email info@mamamagnet.org with a CC to art@sacartamsterdam.com, subject line 'JUGAAD - [Your Contribution]', by 5 September 2026; earlier is better given rolling selection.

Open call details

item.title: Utrecht University: PhD, Media and Democracy in the 1970s (NWO Vidi project)
item.description:
Organisation: Utrecht University, Faculty of Humanities, Department of History and Art History

Location: Utrecht, Netherlands (Drift 6)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 36 to 40 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 18-month initial contract, extended to four years after a positive first-year assessment

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

Fully funded PhD position in the NWO-funded Vidi project 'Democracy and the (de-)regulation of the media in Europe since the 1970s', which reads the contestation and transformation of democracy in the last quarter of the twentieth century through media governance. This sub-project examines how social movements, pirate broadcasters and alternative media initiatives challenged the public broadcasting monopoly across Western Europe during the long 1970s, drawing on archival research. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in history or a related field, a demonstrated interest in the history of democracy and media governance, professional English plus at least one other European language, archival research experience and a collaborative approach. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 5535). Project leader Dr Pepijn Corduwener (p.corduwener@uu.nl). Deadline 6 September 2026.

item.title: University of Amsterdam: PhD, Protest and Political Speech in the Nordics 1930-1970 (Sound of Disagreement)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Amsterdam (UvA), Faculty of Humanities, Department of European Studies

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Kloveniersburgwal 48)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 38 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 48 months full-time (16-month initial contract, extended by 32 months after a positive evaluation); preferred start 1 January 2027

Deadline: Closed 20 Aug 2026

Fully funded four-year PhD position within 'The Sound of Disagreement: Embodied Histories of Political Speech 1800-present', an interdisciplinary project on how political groups have argued in public and how disagreement sounds. This sub-project covers Nordic labour movements and the articulation of protest from roughly 1930 to 1970, explicitly working on the sonic practices of political debate and the mediatization of protest, so it suits researchers with a sound studies, media studies or oral history angle as much as historians. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in History, European Studies, Media Studies, Nordic Studies or a related discipline; fluency in Danish, Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish depending on the chosen case study; professional English; archival research skills; and a collaborative disposition. Apply via the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 15290) with a motivation letter, CV and research statement. Deadline 20 August 2026.

item.title: Mondriaan Fund: Inside-Out Art Museum Residency 2027 (Beijing)
item.description:
Organisation: Mondriaan Fund / Inside-Out Art Museum

Location: Beijing, China. For visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, funded by the Mondriaan Fund.

Award: Subsidy of EUR 8,478 for an artist or EUR 5,622 for a curator/critic toward travel, material and living costs (a 10 percent personal contribution is automatically deducted by the Mondriaan Fund); studio, living space and Inside-Out Art Museum support are paid directly by the Mondriaan Fund. For a selected duo the total is increased proportionally to cover the second applicant's travel and accommodation. Contribution for Caribbean-based residents can be increased for higher travel costs. No application fee.

Duration: Three months: 1 March to 30 May 2027 (flexible start date, set by IOAM in consultation with the resident)

Deadline: 27 Aug 2026

Mondriaan Fund-supported working period at Inside-Out Art Museum (IOAM) in Beijing, one of China's leading independent platforms for contemporary art and research. The museum combines exhibitions, critical inquiry and public programmes, giving residents room for in-depth research, experimentation and exchange within a Chinese art scene that is otherwise hard to access from Europe. The residency is framed as cultural exchange rather than production to deadline: IOAM works with a flexible model that takes the resident's other obligations into account and sets the exact start date in consultation with the selected candidate. WHO: visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. Duos and collaborations may apply (two artists, two curators/critics, or a combination who structurally make work together, submitting a joint plan for the work period that leads to a single result, and who live and work together in the same space during the residency), but each individual must submit a separate application; the apartment is well suited to duos or partnerships. WORK PERIOD: one period of three months, 1 March to 30 May 2027, with room for one artist or duo; you can state a preference for the work period in the application form. Selection is by advisory committee; read the Mondriaan Fund Residency explanation for the conditions, assessment and checklist, plus the fund's general terms and conditions, before applying. DEADLINE: Thursday 27 August 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time / 10:00 Caribbean time.

item.title: University of Twente: Postdoc, Multimodal Conversational AI for Cultural Heritage
item.description:
Organisation: University of Twente, Human Media Interaction group

Location: Enschede, Netherlands

Award: EUR 3,546 to 5,538 gross per month for 40 hours per week (8 salary steps, depending on experience), plus standard Dutch university holiday and year-end allowances.

Duration: One year, renewable for a further two years subject to positive evaluation; 40 hours per week

Deadline: Closed 16 Aug 2026

A postdoctoral position in the Human Media Interaction group at the University of Twente on the project 'Balancing Personalisation and Polyvocality: Dialogic Interaction for Open-mindedness and Empathy in Conversational AI'. The work develops and evaluates multimodal conversational agents for museum settings that hold personalisation in tension with exposure to plural perspectives, rather than optimising for engagement alone. Tasks include building models that use gaze, speech and dialogue data to infer visitor engagement and openness, designing adaptive dialogue strategies, running VR-based user studies, and publishing in strong venues. Of the current Dutch academic postings this is the closest thing to a funded creative-technologist brief: museum interpretation, multimodal sensing and dialogue design in one role. REQUIREMENTS: a PhD in computer science, AI, HCI or a related field; experience with conversational AI, dialogue systems or adaptive systems; experience running empirical research, preferably user studies; strong analytical and academic writing skills; and excellent English. Apply with a CV including publications, a motivation letter and two academic references. Contact: Shenghui Wang (shenghui.wang@utwente.nl). NOTE: the AcademicTransfer listing page shows a 16 August 2026 deadline while the detail page states 17 August 2026, so treat 16 August as the effective cut-off.

item.title: University of Groningen: Lecturer 4, Arts, Culture and Media
item.description:
Organisation: University of Groningen, Faculty of Arts

Location: Groningen, Netherlands (Broerstraat 5)

Award: EUR 3,706 to 5,760 gross per month at 1.0 FTE (the post is 0.8 FTE), plus standard Dutch university holiday and year-end allowances.

Duration: Temporary, 12-month fixed-term appointment at 0.8 FTE, starting 1 September 2026

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

A one-year teaching appointment in the Faculty of Arts at the University of Groningen, covering courses across the BA in Arts, Culture and Media and the Popular Music and Sonic Cultures master's track. Teaching spans audiovisual arts, popular music and arts management at both undergraduate and postgraduate level. This is a teaching-weighted post rather than a research one, so it suits practitioners who want a formal academic foothold in audiovisual and sonic culture without committing to a research track. REQUIREMENTS: a research master's in an appropriate arts discipline, undergraduate teaching experience, and English at C1 (CEFR). PREFERRED: a PhD in an appropriate arts discipline, a BKO or UTQ teaching qualification, postgraduate teaching experience, musicology expertise, Dutch at B2, and familiarity with the Dutch higher education system. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy ID V26.2320-EN). Closes 15 August 2026; appointment starts 1 September 2026.

item.title: GLINA3: Open Call for a Collaborator Working with Type, Language and Visual Systems
item.description:
Organisation: GLINA3

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (studio is Amsterdam-based; collaboration terms not specified)

Award: Paid collaboration. The studio states the fee will be confirmed upon successful funding, so the amount is contingent and not published up front. No application fee.

Duration: New collaborative research project, length not specified

Deadline: Closed 12 Aug 2026

GLINA3 is an Amsterdam clay 3D printing and digital design studio, and it is looking for one collaborator to join a new research project at the intersection of typography, language, technology and material culture. They want an artist, writer, poet, anthropologist or artistic researcher whose existing practice already engages with type design, typography, writing systems, visual language, fonts and letterforms, language technologies, or the tools that shape how language is produced, read or translated. This is an unusually good fit for anyone working on the machine-readable side of language: the brief explicitly names language technologies and translation tooling alongside classical type design. ELIGIBILITY: individual practitioners with demonstrable work in one or more of the listed areas. HOW TO APPLY: the studio asks for relevant work, research, publications or projects connected to type, fonts, writing systems, visual language or the tools that shape them, and nothing else. Because the deadline is tight they say Instagram DM is the fastest route; you can also email a short introduction and one relevant project to office@glina3.nl. NOTE: the fee is confirmed only if the project's own funding comes through, so clarify terms before committing time.

Open call details

item.title: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences: Digital Life Researcher (Embodied AI Rehabilitation Agents)
item.description:
Organisation: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (Hogeschool van Amsterdam)

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Weesperzijde campus), on site

Award: EUR 3,064.08 to 4,084.93 gross per month for 40 hours per week, plus an 8.3 percent year-end bonus and 8 percent holiday allowance.

Duration: Full-time, 40 hours per week

Deadline: Closed 30 Jul 2026

A junior researcher post in the Digital Life research group at the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences, working on embodied AI rehabilitation agents that support patients during rehabilitation and recovery in everyday life. The programme sits at the intersection of human-centred AI, digital health and rehabilitation technology, and the role is unusually hands-on for a research job: co-designing rehabilitation technologies with patients and healthcare professionals, building interactive prototypes with sensing technologies and embodied interaction, running user-centred evaluations in real-world living lab settings, and contributing to scientific reports and presentations. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in human-computer interaction, industrial design, computer science, software engineering, AI or a related field; demonstrated research experience including co-design and evaluation with diverse stakeholders; experience designing interactive prototypes with sensing or embodied systems; sensor data collection, processing and analysis skills; and programming in Python, JavaScript or comparable languages. Excellent written and spoken English is required and Dutch proficiency is preferred. Apply with a CV and motivation letter through the application portal. Contact: Bin Yu (b.yu@hva.nl, 0638347028) or vacatures@hva.nl. Closes 30 July 2026.
